per_piece.evidence: By design: cold_9300/NOTES.md:21-22 '10 metadata files, read key by key: timestamps, the workspace's path, the bake's timings, and the hashes and sizes of the files above' -- records of when and where, which differ because the run did.

proposed_status: *STATUS: ANALYSIS 2026-10-22 -- the subject is fixed and proven twice, and what two runs of one command still disagree on is the engine's and the records'. The roof props: Zoo 1.109.0 (c2edb80) restarts every face `bevel_edges` leaves at its lowest vertex with its corner data (zoo/zoo_keeper/bpylayer/geometry.py:111-130, called at :406), and cold runs 9299 and 9300 built every one of the package's 596 GLBs and the lightmap to the same bytes (docs/cold_runs/cold_9300/NOTES.md:7-15). The applied scene's eleven energies: Lux 0.77.0 (4ce4c85) gives its three rigs `rest()` (lux/addons/lux/runtime/rigs/lux_fluorescent_rig.gd:50, lux_stage_light_rig.gd:58, lux_streetlight_rig.gd:156) and Level Factory 0.208.0 (b8fe4f7) rests every `lux_light_rig` before the pack (level_factory/assets/godot/run_lux_apply.gd:369-382); cold runs 9301 and 9302 read all 12 scenes Godot saves 0 lines apart once its per-save ids are masked (cold_9302/NOTES.md:13-14). Left, and not a task: Godot's own per-save ids (node unique_ids, drawn resource ids) and the metadata that records times, paths and the hashes of those -- 22 of 3,283 files, every one attributed, and read since as '247's residue, 0 lines once masked' (roadmap 20670). A package that must match byte for byte would need the ids normalised after every save; nothing asks for that today.*
notes: Per-piece 'moot' here means 'not a task' (engine behaviour, or a record doing its job), the nearest of the allowed states. ANALYSIS rather than DONE because the residue is not done, it is the engine's: Godot assigns per-save ids on every save, and the comparisons that matter already mask them (docs/findings/roofprops_bytes/per_save_ids*.out.txt; masked_scenes.py in later runs). Not checked: whether Godot 4.7 has any setting that makes those ids stable. If a census that hashes raw package bytes is ever built, it would need masked hashes -- that would be a new item, not this one.
